facts.meaning: The stable server-to-client requests are exactly these. No separate server request exists for stdin approval; the existing command approval request handles both command and writeStdin kinds.

Stable approval requests carry neither additionalPermissions nor availableDecisions.
Both exist only with the experimental capability, so a stable client never sees them.
A command approval can be one-action (accept) or session-scoped (acceptForSession), or amend execpolicy or network policy.
A file-change approval can be one-action or session-scoped.
thread/start has no named permission-profile selector without the experimental capability.
The experimental selector names a profile and is exclusive with the legacy sandbox field.
Approval routing (approvalsReviewer) and the legacy policy and sandbox fields are stable thread/start fields.
A client can ask for configuration, managed requirements and the permission profiles without starting a turn. Whether config/read reports the effective execpolicy is not established by the schema.

config/read can be called without a turnId; it does not require an active turn. The experimental ClientRequest schema is not vendored, so experimental client parameter requirements are deferred to W14b.

The command approval response requires decision, and its union is exactly four string values (accept, acceptForSession, decline, cancel) and two amendment objects (acceptWithExecpolicyAmendment with a string array, applyNetworkPolicyAmendment with a network policy amendment). No integer, untyped or other branch exists.
